page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.xlarge is an x86_64 server instance powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The instance is configured with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1.0 GB per core allocation. It contains no local storage and has no GPU accelerators. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark results indicate average single-core performance but weak multi-core and memory capabilities. The single-core stress-ng score of 1783.99 and Geekbench single-core score of 1345.0 fall into the average category. However, multi-core benchmarks show limitations, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2944.0 and a multi-threaded bzip3 decompression speed of 19.73 GB/sec, which is categorized as poor. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, measuring 28.55 GB/sec for large-block reads and 23.42 GB/sec for large-block writes.

This hardware profile presents a clear tradeoff between dedicated CPU allocation and low memory density. With only 4.0 GB of RAM for 4 vCPUs, memory-intensive workloads will face severe bottlenecks. This low resource density positions the instance as a cost-efficient option for compute tasks that do not require substantial memory footprints. It is suitable for lightweight single-threaded tasks, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving, but is poorly suited for database operations, software compilation, or large-scale multi-threaded processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m1.xlarge is an x86_64 virtual server featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 4.0 GB of RAM, powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon processor. It has no local storage or GPU accelerators, and operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps. Performance benchmarks show average single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1345.0, but weak multi-core and memory performance, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 2944.0 and a large-block memory read bandwidth of 28.55 GB/sec. The 1.0 GB per core memory allocation represents a significant tradeoff, limiting the instance's utility for memory-heavy applications. This server is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and low-traffic web serving where dedicated CPU resources are required but memory demands are minimal.
